questions.question: A 2017 paper titled 'Attention Is All You Need' replaced recurrence with self-attention so whole sequences could be processed in parallel — the architecture now behind GPT and BERT. Name it.
questions.explanation: The transformer architecture, built on attention instead of recurrence, underpins modern LLMs.

questions.question: A lab measures one qubit and its distant partner's state instantly correlates no matter the separation — what Einstein called 'spooky action at a distance.' Name this quantum phenomenon.
questions.explanation: Entangled particles share correlated measurement outcomes regardless of distance.

questions.question: While a classical bit is strictly 0 or 1, a register of 3 qubits can represent all 8 values at once until it is measured. Which quantum property makes this possible?
questions.explanation: Superposition lets each qubit hold a combination of 0 and 1, so n qubits encode 2^n states at once.

questions.question: In 2019 Google reported its Sycamore chip sampled a circuit in about 200 seconds that a top supercomputer would need millennia for — the contested milestone where quantum outruns classical on a task. Name it.
questions.explanation: The claimed milestone — a quantum device solving a classically infeasible problem — is quantum supremacy, also called quantum advantage.

questions.question: Bitcoin miners race to find a nonce that makes a block hash begin with enough leading zeros, deliberately burning electricity so cheating costs more than honesty. Name this consensus mechanism.
questions.explanation: Proof of work makes block production computationally costly, securing the chain against forgery.

questions.question: After Ethereum's 2022 Merge, validators lock up 32 ETH as collateral and are chosen to propose blocks instead of racing hashes, cutting energy use by about 99%. Name this consensus mechanism.
questions.explanation: Proof of stake selects validators by staked collateral rather than computational work.

questions.question: A user logs in with a fingerprint; the site stores only a public key while the private key never leaves the phone, so a phishing page captures nothing reusable — a FIDO2 credential. What is it called?
questions.explanation: Passkeys are FIDO-based public-key credentials resistant to phishing and password theft.

questions.question: Starlink achieves ~25 ms latency by flying satellites around 550 km up instead of at geostationary altitude of 35,786 km. In which orbital band do these constellations operate?
questions.explanation: Satellites at a few hundred kilometers altitude are in low Earth orbit, enabling low-latency broadband.

questions.question: A lab announces its new model 'has 70 billion' of these learned numeric weights, and both memory needs and capability scale with their count. What are they?
questions.explanation: An LLM's learned weights are its parameters, commonly counted in billions.

questions.question: A research chip like Intel's Loihi uses spiking circuits that mimic neurons and synapses, drawing power only when 'neurons' fire rather than running a constant clock. Name this brain-inspired approach.
questions.explanation: Neuromorphic designs emulate biological neurons and spikes for ultra-efficient computation.

questions.question: A hospital wants a cloud service to compute statistics on patient records without ever decrypting them — the math runs directly on ciphertext and results decrypt correctly. Name the technique.
questions.explanation: Homomorphic encryption permits computation on ciphertext, keeping raw data hidden from the processor.

questions.question: A keyboard app improves its next-word model across millions of phones while every user's typing data stays on-device — only model updates are uploaded and aggregated. Name this training approach.
questions.explanation: Federated learning trains shared models from on-device updates without centralizing raw data.

questions.question: A blockchain splits its state so groups of nodes each process only their slice of transactions in parallel instead of every node doing everything. Name this scaling technique.
questions.explanation: Sharding partitions data and work across node groups for parallel throughput.

questions.question: A doorbell camera detects packages on an onboard NPU; no footage leaves the house and alerts keep working when the internet drops. What is running models on-device like this called?
questions.explanation: Edge AI runs inference locally on the device rather than sending data to the cloud.

questions.question: A video editor's browser version runs C++ codecs at near-native speed through a compact binary instruction format that every browser's sandboxed VM executes. Name it.
questions.explanation: WebAssembly (Wasm) is a portable binary format enabling near-native code execution in browsers.

questions.question: Starting in late 2024, models like OpenAI's o1 and DeepSeek-R1 improved answers by spending extra computation on step-by-step reasoning during generation rather than only during training. What is this scaling paradigm called?
questions.explanation: Test-time (inference-time) scaling trades longer reasoning chains at generation time for higher-quality answers instead of just scaling training compute.

questions.question: Which Chinese AI lab released the open R1 reasoning model in January 2025, rivaling top US models at a fraction of the reported training cost and triggering a tech stock sell-off?
questions.explanation: DeepSeek's R1 matched leading reasoning benchmarks cheaply, shaking markets and intensifying debate over chip export controls.

questions.question: What is the term for LLM-based systems that autonomously plan steps, call tools and APIs, and complete multi-step tasks — the dominant AI product trend of 2024-2025?
questions.explanation: Agentic systems loop over reasoning and tool use to act on a user's behalf rather than merely answering a single prompt.

questions.question: Which Google quantum chip, unveiled in December 2024, showed error rates falling as more qubits were added — a key milestone toward fault-tolerant quantum computing?
questions.explanation: Willow achieved 'below-threshold' quantum error correction, where scaling up physical qubits reduces rather than increases errors.

questions.question: A 7-billion-parameter model needs about 14 GB in 16-bit storage, but a phone has only ~4 GB free; storing each weight at 4-bit precision shrinks it to roughly 3.5 GB so it fits. Name this precision-reduction technique.
questions.explanation: Quantization reduces weight precision (e.g., FP16 to INT4), cutting size about 4x — 14 GB becomes ~3.5 GB.
